item.content:encoded:
The NBA has announced a one-game suspension without pay for Hawks guard Kingston Flemings, per an official press release (via Twitter).

The suspension stems from an incident that occurred late in the fourth quarter of Atlanta’s game against the Pelicans on Saturday, when the rookie point guard elbowed Pelicans wing Bryce McGowens in the head. Flemings and McGowens were behind the play as New Orleans brought the ball up the floor, with neither of them involved in the play (Twitter video link).

The eighth overall pick in the 2026 Draft, Flemings has quickly established himself as an important part of the Hawks’ second unit, averaging 7.1 points and 4.6 assists in 20.3 minutes per game as a reserve while knocking down 38.5% of his three-point tries.

Flemings will serve the suspension in Monday’s game against the Pacers. The one-game ban will cost him $42,234, which is 1/174th of his $7,348,680 salary for the 2026/27 season, notes ESPN’s Bobby Marks (Twitter link).

item.title: Thunder Exercise Options On McCain, Sorber, Will Decline Topic’s

item.content:encoded:
The Thunder made several contract decisions on Sunday ahead of the November 2 deadline.

Oklahoma City exercised its rookie scale team options on big man Thomas Sorber and guard Jared McCain for the 2027/28 season, the team announced in a press release (Twitter link via Rylan Stiles of SI.com), but will not pick up its option on guard Nikola Topic, per Justin Martinez of The Oklahoman (Twitter link).

Sorber’s third-year option for next season is worth $5.12MM, while McCain’s fourth-year option is for $6.78MM.

With the Thunder affected by injuries up and down their lineup, McCain has become an important part of the club’s rotation. He’s averaging 10.8 points in 24.7 minutes this season and has started three of his four games. The former Sixer was acquired in a trade-deadline deal in February.

Sorber has yet to play a game with Oklahoma City after missing his rookie season with a torn ACL in his right knee and then undergoing another knee procedure in July that has kept him sidelined thus far in the 2026/27 season.

Like Sorber, Topic missed his rookie season due to an ACL tear. He was subsequently limited to just 10 games in 2025/26 after going through chemotherapy for testicular cancer and hasn’t played yet in ’26/27 after undergoing a lumbar microdiscectomy over the summer.

The choice to decline the $7.48MM option on Topic projects to save the Thunder around $60MM based on their current 2027/28 cap outlook, notes Martinez (via Twitter), given how far into luxury tax territory they project to be. According to Martinez, the decision should be viewed as a financial one rather than signaling that Oklahoma City no longer believes in Topic as a prospect.

Topic will now become an unrestricted free agent next summer, at which time the Thunder – or his new team, if he’s traded – will be prohibited from offering him a starting salary exceeding his $7.48MM option.
